title: Write Like a Scribe
sub: Grades 1–2 · Your Name in Hieroglyphs · Signs, sounds and a royal oval

hero.credit: Hans Hillewaert, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons

objective: Children will find that the little pictures carved on the Rosetta Stone are writing, called hieroglyphs, and that many signs stand for sounds: an owl for *m*, a lion for *l*. Using the chart from the exhibition’s *Your Name in Hieroglyphs* room, they will read short words, then write their own names inside a cartouche, the oval that ringed the names of Egypt’s kings and queens.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Hieroglyphs look like pictures, but most of the signs we use today stand for sounds. Knowing that turns a wall of birds, snakes and loaves into words we can read.

items.text: say what some hieroglyph signs are pictures of, and the sound each one stands for
items.question: say what a sign shows, and the sound it stands for?
items.screen: say what a sign shows, and its sound

items.text: read a short word written in hieroglyphs, using the chart
items.question: read a word written in hieroglyphs?

items.question: write your name in a cartouche, with its end line?
items.screen: write my name in a cartouche

items.text: explain that our chart is a modern sound-alike: an Egyptian scribe wrote only the consonants

materials: Page 3 of this plan, projected or printed: the stone, the first eight signs and King Ptolemy’s cartouche
The whole sign chart, on page 1 of every handout
Differentiated handouts, one per child; pencils and crayons in gold, yellow or orange
questions: Which sign is a lion? Which is an owl? What sound does each stand for?
Where is the line that marks the end of the name?
Which way is the lion facing? Which way do we read?
Why do you think only kings and queens had their names ringed by an oval?
connection: **Virtual visit:** in *Your Name in Hieroglyphs*, type a name and watch it appear sign by sign in a cartouche, see how a scribe might write it with consonants only, and print it.
**Next:** in *The Rosetta Stone Decoder*, older children use the Greek to crack King Ptolemy’s name.

steps.title: A stone full of pictures
script: Show the top of the stone on page 3. Ask: *“What pictures can you find carved here?”* Children call out birds, people, snakes, loaves. Then ask them to find an **oval** with signs inside it.
*“These pictures are writing. They are called hieroglyphs. This stone was carved more than two thousand years ago, in Egypt.”*

img.credit: Hans Hillewaert, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons

screen.alt: The top of the Rosetta Stone: rows of tiny carved hieroglyphs, birds, people, snakes and loaves, on dark gray stone, with an oval ringing a few signs
screen.caption: The top of the Rosetta Stone

steps.purpose: Look before anyone explains: find the pictures, and the oval.
students: Find a bird. Find a person. Find a snake.
Can you find an oval with signs inside it?

steps.title: A picture for a sound
script: Show the first eight signs on page 3. *“Each sign is a picture of something, but it stands for a sound. The owl says* m*. The lion says* l*.”* Play a quick game: say a sound and children point to its sign; point to a sign and they say its sound.

screen.caption: Eight signs from the chart
columns: The sign is a picture of

steps.purpose: Meet the first signs: each is a picture, and each stands for a sound.
students: Which sign is a lion? What sound does it make?
I say a sound. You point to its sign.

steps.title: A name in an oval
script: Read the room’s own words: *“In ancient Egypt, the names of kings and queens were written in hieroglyphs. Each royal name was ringed by an oval, called a cartouche.”* Show the room on the screen and King Ptolemy’s name on page 3. Children find the lion and the loaf of bread. Point out the straight **line** at one end: it marks the end of the name.

screen.alt: The Your Name in Hieroglyphs room: the name Cleopatra in gold signs inside a cartouche, each sign above its letter, and below it the same name written with consonants only
screen.caption: Your Name in Hieroglyphs: a name, sign by sign, inside a cartouche

steps.purpose: See a name written sign by sign, inside a cartouche with its end line.
students: Find the lion. What sound is it?
Find the line at the end of the oval.

steps.title: Which way to read
script: *“Which way do we read?”* Look at the people and animals: if they face right, read from right to left. (Signs could also run in columns, always top to bottom.) On our handouts the animals face left, so we read left to right.

screen.text:
Look at the people and animals.
If they face right, read from right to left.

steps.purpose: Learn the way to read: follow the faces.
students: Which way does the owl face?

steps.title: Read it together
script: Read one word together, sign by sign, from the chart: a ripple of water (*n*), a reed (*i*), a lion (*l*), two reeds (*e*). *“N, I, L, E: Nile,”* Egypt’s great river.

screen.question: A ripple of water, a reed, a lion, two reeds. What word is it?

steps.purpose: Read one word together before working alone.
students: Find each sign on the chart.
Say its sound. Put the sounds together.

steps.title: Your handout

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Match four signs to the pictures they show, read *CAT* with the first letter given, then copy their name sign by sign into a cartouche and draw its end line.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: Read two words with the chart, write their name in a cartouche with its end line, and circle which way to read.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Read three words, write their name in a cartouche, then write it again the scribe’s way with the vowels left out, and write a secret word for a partner.

steps.purpose: Read and write hieroglyphs on paper, at the right level of challenge.
students: All three end with your own name in a cartouche.

steps.title: Look back
script: Ask the objectives back as questions, from the screen or page 1: *“Can you now…?”* For each one, children show a thumb up, sideways or down. For the last, ask a Red Level child.

screen.hint: Show me: thumb up, sideways or down.

steps.purpose: Check what each student can now do against the objectives.
students: say what a sign shows, and the sound it stands for?
read a word written in hieroglyphs?
write your name in a cartouche, with its end line?
say what an Egyptian scribe would leave out?

steps.title: The scribe’s way
script: Show the room again, with its second cartouche. *“An Egyptian scribe would have left the vowels out, writing only the consonants.”* Ask: *“Say your name the scribe’s way, with the vowels left out.”* Children try it with a partner.

screen.question: Say your name the scribe’s way, with the vowels left out.

steps.purpose: End with what a real scribe would do: write the consonants only.
students: Say your name without its vowels.
Does it still sound like you?
